A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReasonEdit study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original editing experiments on FVQA and A-OKVQA across four VLMs, sequential-editing results, and ablation and embedding analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original editing experiments and adds empirical noise-robustness, component-ablation, embedding-selection, and patch-quality results.

M1.justification: The codebook, visual patchification, key merging, dual embedding, and retrieval procedures remain unchanged. The explicit yes/no patch filter, descriptive scoring prompt, and 90%/10% merging thresholds added to the main explanation already appear in v1 Appendix C.

E1.justification: FVQA and A-OKVQA remain the editing benchmarks. v4 adds Flickr30k images for embedding-selection validation in Appendix A.3 and introduces editing scenarios with injected or replaced irrelevant reasoning, extending source and input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: IKE-COT newly participates in both Table 1 comparisons and sequential-editing Figure 12; v1 reports the other COT variants but no IKE-COT results. The five base editors remain. New Table 3 also introduces ground-truth answer and reasoning prompting controls.

E3.justification: New studies introduce 10%, 30%, and 50% reasoning injection/replacement protocols, answer-only and reasoning-only conditions with oracle-prompt controls, CLIP similarity evaluation, and source-specific embedding selection. These substantially extend the evaluation design. The original four VLMs, editing metrics, and sequential evaluation every 200 edits on 50 sampled edits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds tests of noisy feedback, the separate contributions of answer and reasoning entries, sensitivity to embedding-selection data, automatic patch quality, and alternative layer-selection criteria (Tables 2–5 and 7). These substantially broaden mechanism and robustness checks. Existing embedding, retrieval-parameter, and key-merging ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 4 replaces separate VLM trajectories with averages across VLMs and shaded bands, changing variability reporting for sequential editing. The bands are not statistically defined. The existing B=10 Monte Carlo sampling and bias mean/standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged; no additional seeds or repeated-run counts are documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises IKE scores while preserving every other existing result row. For A-OKVQA with LLaVA-1.5-7B, IKE accuracy changes from 0.27 to 0.97 and image generality from 0.34 to 0.95 under unchanged reported settings; the cause is unstated. IKE-COT and the new robustness, component, selection, and patch-quality studies add substantial results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, embedding-selection objectives, scale-invariance proofs, and sample-size derivations are retained. v1 Appendices A.3–A.4 correspond to v4 A.4–A.5. Expanded main-text explanations and the empirical source-selection study introduce no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: human-reasoning-based VLM editing, topology-guided embeddings, state-of-the-art editing, and improved generalization with locality and efficiency. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v4 adds explicit limitations concerning codebook search costs and inaccurate or incomplete human reasoning. It interprets replacement-noise degradation as loss of relevant facts, distinguishes answer and reasoning contributions, and interprets source-stable hyperparameters as evidence of largely data-agnostic selection. These extend the retained retrieval-based explanation.

D1.justification: The future-release promise becomes a statement that code and data are available through a repository link. v4 also documents source-specific layer indices and weights, combined-dataset ablations, and filtering counts of 389 A-OKVQA and 74 FVQA images. Repository availability is reported by the PDF, not independently verified.

R1.justification: v4 adds Plummer et al. (2015) for Flickr30k. Appendix A replaces the assertion that prior embedding choices lacked quantitative justification with the narrower description that they were selected through post hoc editing-performance ablations. The broader positioning against previous editors remains.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized language corrections, expands motivation and method explanations, adds subsections, and numbers and reorders the ablation discussion. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain. Publication and correspondence information also change.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation expands with new robustness and component tables in the main text and selection and patch-quality tables in the appendices. Table 1 gains IKE-COT rows, Figure 4 is redrawn using averages and bands, and Figure 12 adds IKE-COT series. Retained figures are resized or relocated; v1 Table 2 becomes v4 Table 6.

improvement.justification: Table 3 addresses an important missing control in v1 by separating reasoning contributions from answer storage, directly strengthening evidence for the central contribution. Noise and design-validation studies test additional assumptions, while IKE-COT comparisons and explicit limitations improve assessability. Unexplained IKE revisions, undefined uncertainty displays, and differing noise-free controls in Table 2 remain weaknesses, but the added controls provide a substantial net gain.
